description: We are a software engineering and analytics squad from Peshawar tackling "Be an Earth System Trend Detective!" We are building an interactive web platform that mines 25+ years of NASA satellite observations to verify statistical climate shifts, regional anomalies, and precipitation trends with a focus on delivering a high-impact, live web tool.
summary:
GeoPulse Analytics is a zero-download, browser-based Earth System Trend Detective workbench built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Using Next.js, MapLibre GL, and a Python/SciPy serverless engine, it transforms 45 years of NASA Earth observation records (1981–2025) into statistically rigorous regional trend comparisons in under two seconds.

Instead of downloading gigabyte NetCDF files, GeoPulse streams lightweight (<15 KB) JSON time series from the NASA POWER API (MERRA-2/GLDAS) alongside live NASA GIBS satellite layers. A 2-step Detective Wizard translates plain-English environmental questions into curated NASA variables, while side-by-side Pin A vs. Pin B selection uncovers Regional Divergence—such as statistically significant soil wetting in Pakistan's Upper Indus (p = 0.0090) versus non-significant drift in Balochistan (p = 0.2787). To prevent single-year outliers like the 2022 floods from skewing results, GeoPulse pairs OLS regression with outlier-resistant Theil–Sen slopes, Mann–Kendall significance testing, autocorrelation caveats, and an evidence-first AI interpreter linked directly to NASA Giovanni and CUAHSI.

This matters because national averages hide local climate extremes, and GeoPulse empowers students, educators, and planners to separate real climate signals from weather noise without specialized GIS tooling.
details:
GeoPulse Analytics is a zero-download, browser-based Earth System Trend Detective workbench built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Inside a single-screen interface, users either launch pre-verified "Golden Case Files" or use a 2-step Detective Wizard to turn plain-English questions into curated NASA variables. By placing two pins on an interactive MapLibre GL canvas overlaid with live NASA GIBS satellite imagery (SMAP, AIRS, GPM, OMI, MODIS), the platform pioneers Side-by-Side Regional Divergence Mode, fetching lightweight (<15 KB) JSON time series from the NASA POWER API (MERRA-2 and GLDAS, 1981–2025) to compare two regions in under two seconds.

Built with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and a Python/SciPy serverless backend on Vercel, GeoPulse is designed for both statistical rigor and accessibility. Because single extreme events—like Pakistan's 2022 super-flood—can skew standard OLS averages, our team paired OLS regression with the outlier-resistant Theil–Sen median slope and non-parametric Mann–Kendall significance test, alongside 95% confidence intervals, lag-1 autocorrelation warnings, and Annual/Monsoon/Winter seasonal filters. An evidence-first AI interpreter translates only verified SciPy outputs into plain English (with a deterministic offline fallback), backed by reproducible Markdown/PDF exports and 1-click verification links to NASA Giovanni, Worldview, and CUAHSI.

Its intended impact is to eliminate gigabyte NetCDF downloads, login walls, and complex GIS tooling so students, educators, and local planners can separate real climate signals from weather noise. By exposing localized extremes hidden behind national averages—such as significant soil wetting in Pakistan's Upper Indus (p = 0.0090) versus non-significant drift in Balochistan (p = 0.2787)—GeoPulse makes 45 years of NASA Earth science immediately actionable for anyone.
